---
title: "Shared Part II supplied-trial memory and execution time"
format: html
---

Issue [#368](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/368)
changes result retention as well as supplied-trial construction. The comparison
base is `1cb771e`. No equation, tolerance, supplied composition, Engine source,
parameter adoption or manuscript changes.

## Bounded work and complete disk records

`Route.grid()` passes one supplied inventory to the state workers. The executor
submits windows of at most four states per worker: 12 states with three workers.
Each worker constructs native trials for its current state. Exact equal kind,
ordered support, full composition and packing share an Engine evaluation;
expansion restores the original trial order and counts, without rounding.

Before returning, each worker writes its complete state record incrementally
through gzip to `search-N/<SHA-256 of state key>.json.gz`. This preserves every
supplied-trial record, Engine cause and support difference in the original
order. The existing `jsonable` conversion applies to one state, including its
established nonfinite diagnostic representation. It never copies or formats
the full detailed search in the parent.

`search-N.json` contains ordered state summaries: counts, minima, availability,
descent classification, required resolved witnesses and a relative `details`
reference. Neither negative nor unavailable supplied-trial lists remain in
memory. Memory still holds state summaries and the required witness registry;
the removed term is the product of states and full supplied-trial records.
Part I's existing state-specific inputs remain supported.

Penalty and retreat consume the same `descent()` and `tally()` quantities from
summaries. Reporting retains unavailable-state causes and detail references.
`Route.result(row['details'])` explicitly reads one complete state when needed.
The next search loads only `split-record.json`, never the detailed search.

## Endpoint search reuse

`fit()` searches the endpoint before `candidate()` asks for its search. Reuse
requires exact equality of the endpoint, ordered states, ordered supplied
inventory and complete route declaration, including controls. The immutable
wheel and the native search scale remain unchanged. Only the last matching
result is reused. The signature and summaries do not contain detailed results.

The full DEA endpoint has identical inputs: its repeated request reused the
first result, with exactly one detailed search and identical summaries. Its
start-state inventory was also checked against the endpoint-state inventory.
A changed supplied inventory invalidated reuse. New resolved witnesses can
therefore make PZ's second search different on purpose; that search still runs.
No unconditional removal of the second search was made.

## Numerical identity and failure preservation

Complete decoded records, excluding `seconds` only, match the retained baseline:
PZ Hilliard 55/56 with all 102 trials each, AMP binary/loaded/failed cases,
six MEA F2 states and all 3,791 DEA states. DEA remains 3,736 available,
55 unavailable and zero splits. Counts, minima and descent classification
also agree between each streamed record and its summary in both memory slices.
The baseline values remain in [caller-results.json.gz](results/caller-results.json.gz)
and [mea-F2-results.json.gz](results/mea-F2-results.json.gz).

The final full suite reports `11 failed, 113 passed, 17 subtests passed in 140.21s (0:02:20)`. Its 11 failure
names exactly match the baseline; the 18 Part II tests pass. The single new test
checks a 67,536-state inventory without eager copying or an unbounded executor
submission. PZ's existing tests read complete records through their references.
A separate streamed probe preserves exact duplicates, support differences and
individual errors. A serialization-only probe preserves the established
`nan`/`inf` strings; these synthetic diagnostics are not physical results.
See [verification.json](results/round1/verification.json).

## Measured memory and compressed disk use

These are computational feasibility measurements, not physical validation.
The installed wheel was compared byte for byte with Engine main
`391dfe5d64ede5036bf160bc6ae037ad5e14af32`, SHA-256
`0962e21d2fa7a8ba1ed4622f1110b3e8053bacd878fa41c999d85e8b9afab66b`.
Every job used `agent-heavy`, three workers and its three-core quota.

MDEA uses the provisional 2,789-trial record and unoptimized first Stage B start
bound to adopted F2 shared values. PZ uses its own grown record (1,860 resolved
trials plus two composition-only trials) and its retained first F2 fit endpoint.
The source #343 and #345 worktrees were read without editing them. MDEA's
transformed snapshot is [provisional-trials.json.gz](results/provisional-trials.json.gz);
PZ's exact snapshot is [pz-input-trials.json.gz](results/round1/pz-input-trials.json.gz).
Neither is a new adoption.

| Measured quantity | MDEA | Piperazine |
|---|---:|---:|
| Slice states | 123 | 63 |
| Supplied trials per state | 2,789 | 1,862 |
| Supplied records evaluated | 331,891 | 117,306 |
| Supplied records unavailable | 11,156 | 0 |
| Supplied records not applicable | 0 | 0 |
| Peak summed RSS, KiB | 548,908 | 397,200 |
| Peak summed RSS, MiB | 536.04 | 387.89 |
| Compressed detail bytes | 55,179,906 | 16,545,358 |
| Mean compressed detail bytes/state | 448617.12 | 262624.73 |
| Summary file bytes | 129,208 | 70,439 |
| Complete search elapsed time, s | 151.9803 | 101.4032 |

The slices select 120 MDEA grid indices or 60 PZ grid indices equally spaced
across each complete grid, including both ends, plus the first, middle and last
data states. Exact keys, classifications and file hashes are retained in the
[measurement results](results/round1/mdea-120.json),
[PZ results](results/round1/pz-60.json) and their `*-files.json` inventories.
All full detailed files remain at the recorded `detail_root` paths; one complete
state for each amine is also retained beside those inventories.

The monitor samples `/proc` every approximately 50 ms, summing parent and
recursive worker RSS and excluding the monitor itself. Shared resident pages
are counted for each process, as requested by summed RSS. These are sampled
maxima, not a continuous peak, a confidence interval or a full-campaign bound.
The monitor spans `Route.grid()`, including worker initialization, compressed
writes, registry update and summary serialization. There was one final run per
slice on a busy shared machine. Preliminary runs are superseded by these final
measurements, which include the per-state `jsonable` conversion.

MDEA's 123-state slice has 118 available searches, five unavailable and one
state with descent. PZ's 63 searches are available and three show descent.
These are finite-search classifications at the named records, not full-grid
split counts or evidence of physical validity. No unavailable search is stable.

## Registry growth and planning consequence

MDEA grew from 2,789 to 2,793 distinct resolved trials; the next search received
all 2,793. The grown PZ slice retained all 1,862 supplied inputs and its eight
resolved-witness occurrences were already in the registry. A separate PZ state
starting from the original inventory grew 100 resolved trials to 104; the next
search received 106 inputs including the two composition-only trials. A guarded
reader recorded only `split-record.json` during that next-search setup.
See [pz-growth.json](results/round1/pz-growth.json).

The complete MDEA inventory is 67,536 grid states, already including both
pressure multipliers, plus 1,563 data states. PZ has 8,640 grid plus 440 data
states. Scaling each final slice's elapsed time and compressed detail bytes by
its complete state count gives the following planning projections:

| Per complete search | MDEA | Piperazine |
|---|---:|---:|
| Wall time at observed three-worker throughput, h | 23.72 | 4.06 |
| Compressed detailed output, GiB | 28.87 | 2.22 |

These are projections, not measured full searches. Failures, domain coverage,
new witnesses, corrected inventories, parameter changes, compression and disk
speed can change them. Earlier native-only batch timing averaged 1.15872 ms
per evaluation on the same pinned wheel; it excludes disk writing and does not
replace the complete-path measurement above. No before/after speed claim is
made from different slices. Reused identical searches avoid another complete
search; new inventories require their own search and disk allocation.

The input and detailed-result Cartesian allocations are removed. The retained
state summaries and required registry still grow with their own cardinalities.
No full MDEA or PZ campaign was launched. Independent re-review remains a merge
gate. The notebook is not promoted for manuscript use and is retained without
site registration because `_cse-manuscript.json` is outside this task.
